reason: The deliverable is a written system-design packet and a stdlib CLI script judged on architecture reasoning and correctness, with no screen or interaction surface where visual prototyping would inform the decision.
summary: Lucas needs a complete, submission-ready packet for SingleGrain's "Real-Time Analytics Pipeline" system-design challenge (engineer-004): a ≤4-page design doc redesigning a martech analytics pipeline from 15-30min-latency/~3%-loss/crash-prone to <5s real-time on AWS (50M+ events/day, 500+ tenants, $50K/mo, 3mo MVP/6mo full, 2 senior engineers, SOC2/GDPR/CCPA, zero data loss), plus a working fixture anomaly-detection script (Python 3.11 stdlib, unittest tests), an evidence log with proof tiers, labeled numbers (observed/estimated/benchmarked/assumed), AI-usage disclosure, failure-modes section, and "what stays human" section — analyzing the fixture's nine identified anomaly classes by event_id and flagging fixture items not to be taken at face value. Work proceeds under an approve/override collaboration model (Claude proposes architecture/decisions with reasoning, Lucas approves or overrides each), grounded in Lucas's real but adjacent experience (queue-based backend systems, PostHog as SDK consumer only), targeting Tier 3/4 rigor via actual local benchmarking of the script against the fixture, with no fixed deadline.
